s: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was God, and the Word became flesh. John the Baptist points to the Lamb of God, and the first disciples follow.
At a wedding in Cana Jesus turns water into wine. He drives the traders out of the temple.
Jesus tells Nicodemus that one must be born again of water and the Spirit. God so loved the world that he gave his only Son.
Jesus speaks with a Samaritan woman at the well about living water, and heals an official's son.
Jesus heals a man at the pool of Bethesda on the sabbath and speaks of his oneness with the Father.
Jesus feeds five thousand and walks on water. He is the bread of life: whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life.
Jesus teaches at the feast of Tabernacles: let anyone who thirsts come to me. The people are divided about him.
Jesus forgives a woman caught in adultery. I am the light of the world. Before Abraham was, I am.
Jesus heals a man born blind, who comes to believe while the Pharisees refuse.
I am the good shepherd, who lays down his life for the sheep. I and the Father are one.
Jesus raises Lazarus from the dead: I am the resurrection and the life. The leaders plot to kill him.
Mary anoints Jesus at Bethany. Jesus enters Jerusalem and says that a grain of wheat must die to bear fruit.
At the Last Supper Jesus washes the disciples' feet and gives a new commandment: love one another as I have loved you.
I am the way, the truth and the life. Jesus promises to send the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete.
I am the vine and you are the branches. No one has greater love than to lay down his life for his friends.
The Spirit will guide you into all truth. Your sorrow will turn into joy.
Jesus prays to the Father for his disciples and for all who will believe, that they may be one.
Jesus is arrested, questioned by Annas and Caiaphas, and denied by Peter. Pilate asks: what is truth?
Jesus is crowned with thorns and crucified. He gives his mother to the beloved disciple and says: it is finished. Blood and water flow from his side.
Mary Magdalene finds the tomb empty and meets the risen Lord. Jesus breathes the Spirit on the apostles. Thomas believes: my Lord and my God.
Jesus appears by the sea of Tiberias. He asks Peter three times, do you love me, and tells him: feed my sheep.

1: The eternal Word of God becomes a man. This is the mystery of the Incarnation.
2: At his mother's request Jesus turns water into wine, his first sign.
3: Perhaps the best-known verse in the Bible: God gives his Son out of love, so that all who believe may have eternal life.
6: Jesus says plainly that his flesh is true food and his blood true drink. Many walk away, but Peter says: Lord, to whom shall we go?
11: Jesus calls his dead friend from the tomb after four days. It foreshadows his own resurrection.
13: The Lord and Master kneels to serve his disciples and tells them to do the same for one another.
19: From the cross Jesus gives his mother to the beloved disciple, and through him to all his followers.
Jesus completes the work his Father gave him and dies on the cross.
20: The risen Jesus breathes the Spirit on the apostles and gives them power to forgive sins. The Church sees here the sacrament of confession.
Doubting Thomas sees the risen Jesus and makes the Gospel's greatest confession of faith.
21: Peter, who denied Jesus three times, now says three times that he loves him, and is given care of the whole flock.
